This guide is aimed at camper-van travellers who care most about **direct lake access, easy SUP launching, attractive pitches, and practical camper access**. It is based primarily on official campsite websites, the official Lake Iseo tourism portal, current 2026 price lists and operating information, supplemented by recent camper and traveller reports where they add practical detail.

## Your trip: 2 September 2026

For **your specific trip** — arriving around **2 September 2026**, travelling in a **medium-sized rented camper van**, **without a dog** and **without your own SUPs** — the most important extra criterion is **rental reliability**, not merely whether a campsite technically owns one or two boards.

### Stay length changes the economics

A departure date has not yet been fixed in this guide, and that matters because several rules are stay-length dependent. Use these two scenarios as a planning shortcut:

| If you stay… | What changes |
|---|---|
| **3 nights: 2–5 Sep** | **Punta d’Oro normally does not fit** its 6–7-night high-season minimum, except if staff can place you into a short gap. **Sassabanek’s 10% September promotion does not apply** because it requires 5+ nights. Quai is already in mid season; its ordinary pitches can meet its normal 3-night advance-booking minimum, while lakefront pitches normally require 4 nights. |
| **7 nights: 2–9 Sep** | **Punta d’Oro’s normal 6–7-night minimum becomes workable** depending on pitch category. **Sassabanek’s 10% September promotion applies.** Covelo’s fourth-row ACSI period has already started. Sassabanek’s ACSI period starts on 6 Sep; ask the campsite whether it can be applied to the qualifying nights of a stay that began earlier. |

For any other duration, use the per-night table below and check the minimum-stay notes before comparing totals.

### Choose your shore

The expanded campsite list now gives four genuinely different bases rather than concentrating almost entirely on Iseo town:

| Area | Best candidates | Why choose it |
|---|---|---|
| **Iseo / south shore** | del Sole, Quai, Punta d’Oro, Sassabanek, Camping Iseo, Covelo | Best concentration of campsites, restaurants, shops and ferry access; several on-site SUP options |
| **Pilzone / east shore** | Pilzone, Cave, Olivella | Compact lakefront cluster with **Lagovivo** as a dedicated SUP/kayak operator within a short walk |
| **Marone / Pisogne / upper lake** | Riva di San Pietro, Eden | More dramatic northern scenery; **Surface SUP Academy**, **RentalKles** and Canottieri Sebino widen the rental options |
| **Predore / southwest shore** | Eurovil | Quieter alternative near Sarnico, with on-site SUP rental plus **Whassup Rental** in Predore |

### Best fit for this trip

1. **Camping Pilzone** — still the best balance of price, genuine lakefront camping and rental reliability. **Lagovivo** is at Via Cave 1, on the same short lakeside strip as the campsite at Via Cave 11. Regional tourism sources say it has SUPs for different ability levels, gives a safety briefing and route advice, supplies buoyancy aids/dry storage, and welcomes phone reservations. A very recent August 2026 review reports renting **four touring SUPs at once without pre-booking** and describes a good quantity/range of boards.
2. **Camping Eurovil (Predore)** — a strong Predore alternative with unusually good rental redundancy. The campsite itself now advertises **SUP rental**, 6A camper pitches, and a **new 2026 camper area with lake view**. The campsite describes itself as a few metres from the lake with **lake access directly in front**; this is slightly different from a first-row pitch that physically touches the shore. Predore also has the dedicated **Whassup Rental** operation as a second SUP option.
3. **Camping del Sole Village** — best zero-friction resort option. SUPs, canoes and pedal boats are rented **directly at the campsite**. The fleet size is not published, so it should not be assumed unlimited, but the operation is a regular on-site service rather than a token pair of boards.
4. **Camping Quai** — on-site SUP and kayak rental with published prices (€10/1h, €18/2h, €25/3h, €32/4h, €37/day for a SUP), and the campsite explicitly recommends reserving equipment **at least one day in advance** at reception. Its mid-season rates also begin on 1 September.
5. **Camping Eden (Pisogne)** — a strong north-lake option. It is directly on the lake, has proper motorhome service infrastructure, and sits on the same Via Piangrande lakeside strip as **Surface SUP Academy's X Beach base**, which publishes a full 2026 SUP rental tariff. The trade-off is a simpler campsite with smaller pitches and rather dated sanitary facilities according to several current reviews.
6. **Sassabanek** — excellent early-September value/facilities combination. Its official Sporting Lido page confirms **SUP and kayak rental**, the Lido remains open through **6 September 2026**, and the campsite's September pitch promotion starts on 1 September.
7. **Camping Punta d’Oro** — arguably the nicest small-site all-round camping experience, but **not the easiest choice for this trip**: the official inventory is only **two SUPs**, and on 2 September its normal high-season minimum is **6 nights for some pitch categories and 7 nights for the lake-area categories**. Shorter stays are possible only when they fit booking gaps. Phone before relying on either the pitch or both boards.
8. **Riva di San Pietro** — strong northern/east-shore base because **Surface SUP Academy** is only a few doors away in Marone and publishes a full 2026 rental tariff with several board categories.
9. **Camping Olivella (Pilzone)** — useful low-cost fallback in the same Via Cave cluster as Pilzone, Cave and Lagovivo. It is genuinely lakefront and its official 2026 tariff is attractive, but current camper reviews contain a specific warning about tight access/parking for larger vehicles, so confirm the exact pitch and access route for the rental camper.
10. **Camping Cave** — almost the same Lagovivo advantage as Pilzone, but Pilzone is the more natural first choice unless Cave's pitch/shade suits you better.
11. **Covelo** — excellent campsite, but no verified on-site SUP rental.
12. **Camping Iseo** — lovely sandy water access but no verified on-site rental, so less convenient for this trip.

**Belvedere Clusane** is retained as a **conditional fallback rather than ranked as a normal touring option**. Its own current site still says it has pitches and stopover areas directly on the lake, but current PiNCAMP data simultaneously reports **zero tourist pitches** and no full motorhome service station. That contradiction is too important to ignore: phone the campsite and confirm that a transient camper pitch is actually bookable before relying on it.

**Rental strategy:** because the trip depends on hired boards, reserve SUPs separately whenever the operator allows it. Quai explicitly recommends day-before equipment reservations; Lagovivo welcomes phone reservations; Punta d’Oro has only two boards and should be called before relying on them.

**Date-specific note:** 2 September is still peak/high season at Punta d’Oro (through 5 September), Pilzone and Cave (through 13 September), Camping Iseo (through 14 September), and **Olivella (through 6 September)**. Del Sole and Quai have already moved into cheaper shoulder-season bands, while Sassabanek starts its September pitch promotion on 1 September. Eurovil is open through 27 September and Eden through 30 September; neither currently exposes a clean official 2 September touring-pitch tariff online.

**ACSI note for these dates:** Covelo's published 2026 ACSI rate begins on 1 September but applies only to its fourth-row category. Sassabanek's ACSI period does **not** start until 6 September, so its relevant benefit on 2 September is the separate September promotion, not ACSI. ACSI cards can now be **physical or digital**; either must be valid and presented/scanned at check-in.

## Prices, booking constraints & availability status — 26 August 2026

**Arrival assumed: 2 September 2026.** You have not yet specified a departure date, so the figures below are primarily **per-night comparisons for two adults and one medium camper**. Where a campsite has a minimum-stay rule or a multi-night promotion, that is shown separately. Tourist tax is included in the comparison where the current official tariff states it clearly; one-off booking fees and optional extras are noted separately.

A limitation is worth stating explicitly: most Lake Iseo campsites do **not** publish a simple live inventory calendar that can be reliably read without completing their interactive booking/enquiry form. Consequently, a blank or non-readable web result is **not evidence of being sold out**, and the guide never labels a site unavailable unless the source actually supports that conclusion. I therefore distinguish between **published 2026 pricing** and **live availability**. I have not removed any campsite merely because availability could not be confirmed online.

| Campsite | Availability for arrival 2 Sep | Approx. price for 2 adults + camper on 2 Sep | What the current booking information means |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **Punta d’Oro** | **Not live-confirmed; enquiry required** | **€49.60–€73.40/night** incl. tourist tax; +€5 booking fee once | Still ALTA 2 through 5 Sep. Normal high-season minimum is **6 nights** for BIANCA/VIOLA/AZZURRA and **7 nights** for BLU/VERDE; shorter stays are considered only when they fill gaps. |
| **Covelo** | **Booking engine live, but exact 2 Sep inventory not publicly readable** | **€52–€63/night** incl. tourist tax | 2 Sep is still in Covelo's highest 27 Jun–7 Sep tariff band. Its 2026 PDF also lists an **ACSI fourth-row rate of €27 from 1 Sep**, but does not spell out all inclusions in that table. |
| **del Sole Village** | **Official booking engine live; exact 2 Sep pitch inventory not exposed in searchable output** | **€49–€55/night** incl. tourist tax, depending on pitch type | 2 Sep falls in the **mid-season** band (30 Aug–27 Sep). Current 2026 official tariff: standard €23, large €25.50, equipped standard €27.50, equipped large €29, plus €12 per adult and €1 tourist tax per adult. |
| **Pilzone** | **Direct enquiry required; no reliable public live pitch calendar found** | **€53 standard / €58 lake-zone / €62 first-row** incl. tourist tax | 2 Sep is high season through 13 Sep. Official site directs enquiries to **campeggiopilzone@gmail.com**. |
| **Eurovil (Predore)** | **Official booking/contact channels are live; exact touring-pitch inventory for 2 Sep is not publicly readable** | **Quote required** — no reliable public 2026 touring-pitch tariff found | Open 27 Mar–27 Sep. Camper pitches have 6A electricity; a new lake-view camper area opened for 2026. On-site SUP rental and lake access in front are verified. |
| **Eden (Pisogne)** | **Direct enquiry / booking required; exact 2 Sep pitch inventory not publicly exposed** | **roughly €46–49/night** as current 2026 high-season comparison pricing for a couple; obtain an exact quote | Direct lakefront, motorhome service point, open through 30 Sep. Current directories differ slightly in how they count pitches but consistently treat it as a substantial touring campsite. |
| **Olivella (Pilzone)** | **Direct contact recommended; no dependable live inventory calendar found** | **about €37 Zone A / €47–50 Zone B incl. tourist tax** | 2 Sep is peak season through 6 Sep. The campsite's own bilingual tariff has a small Italian/English inconsistency for Zone B, hence the range; Zone A is clear. Electricity, showers, hot water and private parking are included. |
| **Camping Iseo** | **Not live-confirmed; direct booking/contact required** | **€62 small / €70 medium / €74 lakefront / €88 XL** incl. electricity and €1 pp tourist tax | Peak tariff remains in force through 14 Sep. No ACSI and no dogs. |
| **Camping Cave** | **Bookable online in general; exact 2 Sep inventory not reliably exposed by the searchable booking page** | **€53 standard / €58 lake-zone / €62 first-row** incl. tourist tax | Same high-season pitch/adult structure as Pilzone; 4A electricity is included in the pitch. |
| **Camping Quai** | **Enquiry by pitch zone; no live availability calendar** | **€48–49 fourth row / €51–52 central / €54–55 XL / €57–58 second row / €61–62 lakefront**, incl. tourist tax and €2–3/day electricity | 2 Sep is **mid season**. Official MID rates are €20 / €23 / €26 / €29 / €33 for those pitch categories respectively, plus €12 per adult. |
| **Riva di San Pietro** | **Not live-confirmed; official site offers “Book now” but no public inventory result** | **about €53/night** for 2 people as a current third-party estimate | Treat €53 as indicative rather than an official quote. The campsite is open through 30 Sep. |
| **Sassabanek** | **September offer is active; exact 2 Sep pitch availability requires a personalised quote** | **€44.35 standard / €47.95 large per night** incl. tourist tax **if staying at least 5 nights** | Official offer gives **10% off the pitch component from 1 Sep–4 Oct** for stays of 5+ nights. Without the offer, roughly €46.50 standard / €50.50 large incl. tourist tax. |

**Belvedere Clusane is deliberately not given a price/availability row as though it were a normal touring campsite.** Its own site says pitches and stopover areas exist, while current PiNCAMP data says zero tourist pitches. Treat it as telephone-verification-only until that conflict is resolved.
